full_text_zh:
[P1] 万亚和野兽
〔德〕邬铎·魏格尔特／著
〔克罗地亚〕薛蓝·约纳科维奇／绘
孔杰／译

GUANGXI NORMAL UNIVERSITY PRESS
广西师范大学出版社

[P2] 万亚和野兽
[德] 邬铎·魏格尔特 / 著
[克罗地亚] 薛蓝·约纳科维奇 / 绘
孔杰 / 译

广西师范大学出版社
·桂林·

[P3] 有一天，小兔子万亚独自出门玩。
一路上，他看到很多新鲜又有趣的东西，
兴奋极了，直到想回家时，才发现自己
已经迷路了。

[P4] “怎么办，怎么办？”万亚十分着急，“找人问问路吧。”
这时，一个身影沿河远远地走了过来，可惜是一只狐狸。万亚哆嗦起来，从小爸爸妈妈就警告他要离狐狸远点儿。
“您好！”反正逃不掉了，万亚壮着胆子跟狐狸打了个招呼，“请问，您知道我的家在哪儿吗？”
狐狸盯着万亚，眼珠转了转。“我也很想知道。”
他说，“你肯定不是一个人住，对吧？”
“嗯，不是。”万亚说，“家里还有爸爸妈妈、叔叔婶婶、爷爷奶奶和99个兄弟姐妹。”
“这样啊！”狐狸眼前一亮，“那好吧，我们得尽快找到你的家。”
此刻，狐狸的脑海里已经飘了上百只烤兔子。

[P5] 就在这时，大灰狼路过，一看见万亚，就忍不住扑了上去。狐狸赶紧大喊一声：“住手！”
大灰狼吃惊地看着狐狸。狐狸马上跟狼解释：
“这只可怜的小兔子迷路了，我们必须帮他找到家。
他的叔叔婶婶、爷爷奶奶、爸爸妈妈和 99 个兄弟
姐妹，都在家里等他回去呢。”
“噢，原来是这样啊。”大灰狼冲狐狸眨了眨眼，
“万亚，赶紧想一想，你到底住在哪儿。事情来得
突然，可我也想出把力。”

[P6] 他们一起上了路。万亚走在最前面，后面跟着狐狸和大灰狼。其实万亚特别害怕，但他心里很清楚，绝不能让那两个家伙看出来。
走了没多远，拐角的地方忽然闪出一只棕熊。
他很不屑地瞟了一眼狐狸和大灰狼。
“都给我待在那儿！”棕熊说，“这是我的兔子！”他把熊掌高高举起——狐狸大喊一声：“住手！”狐狸又向棕熊解释了一遍。
“噢，嗯嗯，原来是这样啊。”棕熊意味深长地说，“那行，我们就帮这个小家伙找到家吧！”
于是，万亚的队伍里又多了一只棕熊。

[P7] “我该怎么办？”万亚想，“现在又多了一只棕熊，看来想逃是没戏了。要是他们跟得没这么紧就好了。”
他们走啊走啊，穿过森林，来到了一户农庄。狐狸有些不安，因为他和农庄的一个大家伙——看家狗波波结过梁子。他们一行蹑手蹑脚地溜过农庄，幸亏没有遇到波波。

[P8] 不过，他们遇到了一伙强盗：黄鼠狼、狗獾、臭鼬和猞猁。棕熊很不乐意与他们同行，强盗们却非常乐意。他们一再说明，他们非常同情万亚，而且十分在意，万亚最终是否能找到自己的家。
“下次见面再告诉你们结果。”棕熊这样建议。
“这可不行！”猞猁一边说一边磨了磨爪子，“我们更想亲眼看到万亚回到自己的家，这样才放心。不然的话，他再迷路，那就更糟糕了。”

[P9] 他们继续向前走。现在，万亚完全不知道自己
在哪里，也不知道该怎么回家。可是，他清清楚楚
地听到，这群野兽的肚子已经饿得咕咕叫了。
“走了这么久，你还没想起回家的路吗？”狐狸
有些不耐烦了。
万亚忽然有了一个点子。他鼓起所有的勇气，
大声地说：“没有，我一点儿也想不起来。说实话，
我根本就不认识这里。我肯定怎么也回不了家了。
你们只能拿我填填肚子，而且，对你们来说，一只
兔子太少了。你们自己商量吧，到底谁来吃我！”

[P10] “都怪狐狸！”棕熊愤愤不平，“要不是他的鬼点子，我们也用不着穿过整个森林。”
“好吧！”猞猁说，“有一只兔子，总比什么都没有强。”
啪！狼一巴掌打在地上。“这么一只小小的兔子，用不了一分钟我就能吃掉。”
“为什么是你？”臭鼬说，“我还在这儿呢！”
“还有我，”黄鼠狼嘀咕着，“你们别把我落下了。”
“想什么呢！”狗獾笑了起来，“这只兔子显然就是我的。”

[P11] 他们吵了起来，谁也不让谁。万亚在一旁看着。
“这样吧！”万亚突然说，“我数到三，你们当中最厉害的那个吃我吧！我就在这儿等着。”
万亚开始大声数数：“一——二——三！”
野兽们愤怒地扑到一起：棕熊冲向臭鼬，猞猁和大灰狼纠缠不休，黄鼠狼扑倒了狗獾。一眨眼的工夫，他们扭成一片，这个场面简直闻所未闻。

[P12] 万亚想都没想，头也不回地溜走了。眼看要跑过农庄，狐狸忽然跳了出来，一把按倒了他。
“你很狡猾，万亚。”狐狸狡黠地说，“可狡猾得还不够。你看，我要独享你这份晚餐了。”

[P13] 万亚吓得浑身发抖。
狐狸正要咬下去，一个声音冒了出来：“住手！”看家狗波波出现了，他正好在附近巡逻。
“我们还有一笔账没清呢！”他对着狐狸咬牙切齿地说。
“我用这只兔子还账！”狐狸赶紧说。
“不行！”波波说，“你至少得挨上一顿揍！”
万亚可不敢等他们商量出结果，噌的一下就跑掉了。他像风一样，穿过田野，钻出森林，越过灌木……

[P14] 忽然，万亚停在了自己家门口。他小心翼翼地
看了看四周，没有发现任何野兽的身影。这时，爸爸从家里跳出来迎接他。
“万亚，”他叫道，“你可算回来了！我们都很担
心你。是不是遇到了什么事？”
万亚想了想，抖了抖耳朵。“没有啊，”他说，“我就出去溜达了一圈。”
其实他心里在想，这个故事说出去，也没人相信。
full_text_en:
[P1] Wanya and the Wild Beast
[Germany] Udo Weigelt / Author
[Croatia] Slobodan Jovanovic / Illustrator
Kong Jie / Translator

GUANGXI NORMAL UNIVERSITY PRESS
Guangxi Normal University Press

[P2] Wanya and the Wild Beast
[Germany] Udo Weigelt / Author
[Croatia] Svetlana Jovanović / Illustrator
Kong Jie / Translator

Guangxi Normal University Press
·Guilin·

[P3] One day, the little rabbit Wanya went out to play alone.
Along the way, he saw many fresh and interesting things,
and was so excited that when he wanted to go home, he realized he had already gotten lost.

[P4] "What should I do, what should I do?" Wanya was very anxious. "Let's ask someone for directions."
At this moment, a figure approached from afar along the river, but it was a fox. Wanya trembled, for his parents had always warned him to stay away from foxes.
"Hello!" Since he couldn't escape anyway, Wanya mustered his courage and greeted the fox. "Excuse me, do you know where my home is?"
The fox stared at Wanya, his eyes darting around. "I'd like to know that too."
He said, "You're not living alone, are you?"
"Well, no," Wanya replied, "I have my parents, uncles and aunts, grandparents, and 99 siblings at home."
"Oh, really!" The fox's eyes lit up. "Well then, we must find your home quickly."
At that moment, the fox's mind was already filled with hundreds of roasted rabbits.

[P5] Just then, the big gray wolf passed by. As soon as he saw Wanya, he couldn't help but pounce. The fox quickly shouted, "Stop!"
The big gray wolf looked surprised at the fox. The fox immediately explained to the wolf: 
"This poor little rabbit is lost. We must help him find his home. 
His uncles, aunts, grandparents, parents, and 99 brothers 
sisters are all waiting for him at home."
"Oh, I see," the big gray wolf said, winking at the fox, 
"Wanya, think quickly—where exactly do you live? This happened 
suddenly, but I'd like to lend a hand too."

[P6] They set off together. Wanya walked in front, with the fox and the big gray wolf following behind. Actually, Wanya was very scared, but he knew clearly he couldn't let those two fellows see it.
They hadn't gone far when a brown bear suddenly appeared around the corner.
He gave the fox and the big gray wolf a disdainful glance.
"Stay right there!" the bear said, "This is my rabbit!" He raised his paw high— the fox shouted, "Stop!" The fox then explained to the bear again.
"Oh, I see, I see, so that's how it is," the bear said meaningfully, "Alright, let's help this little fellow find his home!"
Thus, Wanya's group gained another member: a brown bear.

[P7] "What should I do?" Wanya thought, "Now there's a brown bear too, it looks like escaping is out of the question. If they weren't following so closely, it would be better."
They walked and walked, through the forest, arriving at a farm. The fox was a bit uneasy, because he had a history with a big guy from the farm—the guard dog, Bobo. They crept quietly through the farm, luckily without encountering Bobo.

[P8] However, they encountered a gang of bandits: weasels, badgers, skunks, and lynxes. The brown bear was very unwilling to travel with them, but the bandits were very eager. They kept explaining that they deeply sympathized with Wanya and were very concerned about whether he could eventually find his home.
"We'll tell you the result next time we meet," suggested the brown bear.
"That won't do!" the lynx said, sharpening his claws, "We want to see Wanya return home with our own eyes, only then will we be at ease. Otherwise, if he gets lost again, it would be even worse."

[P9] They continued walking forward. Now, Wanya had no idea where he was, or how to get home. But he could clearly hear the wild animals' stomachs rumbling with hunger.
"After walking this long, haven't you remembered the way home yet?" the fox said, growing impatient.
Wanya suddenly had an idea. He gathered all his courage and shouted: "No, I can't remember at all. To be honest, I don't even recognize this place. I'm definitely never getting home. You can only use me to fill your stomachs, and besides, for you, one rabbit is too little. You decide for yourselves—who will eat me!"

[P10] "It's all fox's fault!" the brown bear grumbled, "If it weren't for his tricky idea, we wouldn't have to cross the whole forest."
"Alright!" said the lynx, "Having one rabbit is better than having nothing at all."
*Thwack!* The wolf slapped the ground. "Such a tiny rabbit— I could eat it in less than a minute."
"Why you?" the skunk said, "I'm still here!"
"And me," muttered the weasel, "Don't leave me behind!"
"What are you thinking?" the badger laughed, "This rabbit obviously belongs to me."

[P11] They started arguing, none of them giving in. Wanya watched from the side.
"Alright then!" Wanya suddenly said, "I'll count to three, and the strongest one among you can eat me! I'll wait right here."
Wanya began counting loudly: "One——two——three!"
The wild animals angrily rushed at each other: the brown bear charged at the skunk, the lynx and the gray wolf tangled together, and the weasel knocked down the badger. In the blink of an eye, they were all tangled up in a chaotic mess, a scene truly unheard of.

[P12] Wanya didn't think twice and slipped away without looking back. Just as he was about to run past the farm, the fox suddenly jumped out and pinned him down.
"You're very cunning, Wanya," the fox said slyly, "but not cunning enough. Look, I'm going to enjoy this dinner all by myself."

[P13] Wanya trembled with fear.
Just as the fox was about to bite down, a voice rang out: "Stop!" The watchdog Bobo appeared, patrolling nearby.
"We still have an old score to settle!" he growled at the fox.
"I'll use this rabbit to pay it off!" the fox hurriedly said.
"No way!" Bobo said, "You at least have to get a good beating!"
Wanya couldn't wait for them to reach a decision. With a sudden burst, he ran off. He raced like the wind, across fields, through the forest, over shrubs...

[P14] Suddenly, Wanya stopped at his own front door. He carefully looked around and saw no sign of any wild animals. At that moment, his dad jumped out of the house to greet him.
"Wanya," he called, "you're finally back! We were all so worried about you. Did something happen?"
Wanya thought for a moment and twitched his ears. "No," he said, "I just went out for a little walk." 
Actually, he was thinking to himself, if he told this story, no one would believe it.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《万亚和野兽》的封面，展示了书名、作者、绘者、译者及出版社信息，画面中有一只白色小兔子和一只躲在树后的灰色小动物，背景是秋日森林。
[P2] 本页为绘本《万亚和野兽》的封面，展示了书名、作者、绘者、译者及出版社信息，画面中有一只白色小兔子和一只躲在树后的灰色小动物，背景是秋日森林。
[P3] 小兔子万亚独自出门玩耍，因沿途看到许多有趣的事物而兴奋，回家时才发现自己迷路了。
[P4] 迷路的小兔子万亚在森林里遇到一只狐狸，虽然害怕，但还是鼓起勇气向狐狸问路。狐狸表面答应帮忙，内心却盘算着要吃掉万亚及其家人。
[P5] 大灰狼路过时想扑向迷路的小兔子万亚，狐狸及时阻止并谎称万亚迷路，需要帮助他回家。大灰狼听后表示愿意帮忙，与狐狸一同假装寻找万亚的家。
[P6] 迷路的小兔子万亚在狐狸和大灰狼的陪同下继续前行，途中遇到一只棕熊。棕熊起初想抓兔子，但在狐狸的解释下，决定加入队伍，一同帮助万亚找家。
[P7] 迷路的小兔子万亚在狐狸、大灰狼和棕熊的陪同下穿过森林，来到一户农庄。狐狸因曾与农庄的看家狗波波结仇而感到不安，一行人蹑手蹑脚地溜过农庄，幸运地没有遇到波波。
[P8] 迷路的小兔子万亚在狐狸、大灰狼和棕熊的陪同下，遇到了黄鼠狼、狗獾、臭鼬和猞猁组成的强盗团伙。棕熊建议等下次见面再告知结果，但强盗们坚持要亲眼看到万亚安全回家，因此决定继续同行。
[P9] 迷路的小兔子万亚在狐狸等野兽的陪同下继续前行，他意识到自己完全迷失了方向，而同伴们因饥饿而变得不耐烦。万亚鼓起勇气，故意说自己完全不认识回家的路，甚至主动提出让野兽们吃掉自己，以此试探他们的反应。
[P10] 迷路的小兔子万亚在狐狸、大灰狼、棕熊、黄鼠狼、臭鼬和狗獾等野兽的陪同下继续前行，同伴们因饥饿而对兔子产生觊觎之心，纷纷争抢这只兔子，气氛紧张。
[P11] 迷路的小兔子万亚为了测试同伴们的真心，故意提议让最厉害的野兽吃掉自己，结果野兽们因争抢而大打出手，场面混乱不堪。
[P12] 小兔子万亚试图逃跑，狐狸突然出现并将其按倒，声称要独享他作为晚餐。
[P13] 看家狗波波出现，阻止了狐狸吃掉小兔子万亚，双方因旧怨对峙，万亚趁机逃跑。
[P14] 迷路的小兔子万亚终于安全回到家，父亲焦急地迎接他，万亚谎称只是出去溜达，内心却觉得没人会相信他经历的冒险。
[P15] 画面中，一只小兔子正沿着一条小路奔跑，背景是起伏的黄色山坡和几棵简笔画风格的树木，天空有淡淡的云朵，整体氛围宁静而开阔，暗示着小兔子正在回家的路上。
